summary: Finland prohibits keeping or breeding the roof rat (Rattus rattus) as a pet. The Supervisory Agency (Lupa- ja valvontavirasto, LVV, the authority for alien-species law) confirmed in writing (June 2026, lawyer Wilma Poutanen) that because R. rattus is not found in the wild in Finland it is an “alien species” under the EU Invasive Species Regulation (1143/2014), and Section 3 of the Finnish Invasive Species Act (1709/2015) forbids keeping, breeding, or otherwise handling an alien species in a manner that allows it to enter the environment. On that basis the agency states it is not allowed to keep R. rattus as a pet or breed it in Finland. This is a species classification, not a welfare rule: the Finnish Food Authority separately confirmed (June 2026) that animal-welfare law sets no permit, registration, or species list for keeping rats, and the Finnish Environment Institute confirmed R. rattus is not a CITES species — but the alien-species prohibition governs and overrides those. Note that R. rattus is on neither the EU Union list nor Finland's national invasive list (Decree 1725/2015): the bar comes from the GENERAL alien-species provision (§3), which applies to every alien species, not from a named listing. Never release a roof rat in Finland.
agency_confirmations: Supervisory Agency (Lupa- ja valvontavirasto, LVV), Nature Conservation Unit, written reply 24 June 2026 (Wilma Poutanen, Lakimies): under the EU Invasive Species Regulation 1143/2014, because R. rattus is not found in the wild in Finland it is an alien species; under Section 3 of the Finnish Invasive Species Act an alien species may not be kept, bred, or otherwise handled in a manner that allows it to enter the environment, so it is not allowed to keep R. rattus as a pet or breed it in Finland.

Finnish Food Authority (Ruokavirasto), Animal Health and Welfare, written reply June 2026: keeping rats as companion or hobby animals requires no permit or registration under the Animal Welfare Act 693/2023 (specified by Government Decree 674/2010). There is currently no list of species allowed or denied as companion animals. A notification of activity is required only at commercial scale: selling or handing over small companion animals (self-bred or not) from at least 7 cages, terraria, or aquaria in regular use, or keeping them at 20 or more (Animal Welfare Act Appendix 2). A wild, living-in-the-wild vertebrate may not be taken into possession.
Finnish Environment Institute (Syke), CITES authority, written reply June 2026: Rattus rattus is not a CITES species and has no CITES requirements.

Finnish Food Authority, import/export, June 2026: movement of pet rodents within the EU, Norway, and Switzerland follows the standard import/export rules; a third-country import (for example from the United States) is handled by the Food Authority's border-control team under the usual rabbit-and-rodent import requirements.

keep.why: The Supervisory Agency (Lupa- ja valvontavirasto), the authority for alien-species law, confirmed in writing (June 2026, lawyer Wilma Poutanen) that R. rattus is an alien species under EU Reg 1143/2014 because it is not found in the wild in Finland, and that Section 3 of the Finnish Invasive Species Act (1709/2015) forbids keeping an alien species in a manner that allows it to enter the environment. The agency's stated position is that it is not allowed to keep R. rattus as a pet in Finland. Animal-welfare law imposes no separate species ban or permit, but it does not override the alien-species prohibition.
keep.governing_law: EU Invasive Species Regulation 1143/2014 (alien-species definition) + Finnish Invasive Species Act 1709/2015 §3 (general prohibition on keeping/breeding/handling an alien species in a manner that allows it to enter the environment). Supervisory Agency (LVV) written reply, June 2026.

breed.why: The Supervisory Agency stated (June 2026) it is not allowed to breed R. rattus in Finland: §3 of the Invasive Species Act names breeding an alien species expressly. The welfare-law notification thresholds for selling self-bred animals are moot because lawful keeping/breeding does not exist.
breed.governing_law: EU Invasive Species Regulation 1143/2014 (alien-species definition) + Finnish Invasive Species Act 1709/2015 §3 (general prohibition on keeping/breeding/handling an alien species in a manner that allows it to enter the environment). Supervisory Agency (LVV) written reply, June 2026.

sell_give.why: Follows from the keeping/breeding prohibition: §3 forbids 'otherwise handling' an alien species in a manner that allows environmental entry, and you cannot lawfully possess R. rattus in Finland to sell, give, or rehome it. The Supervisory Agency did not address transfer separately, but there is no lawful pathway to keep the animal being transferred.
sell_give.governing_law: EU Invasive Species Regulation 1143/2014 (alien-species definition) + Finnish Invasive Species Act 1709/2015 §3 (general prohibition on keeping/breeding/handling an alien species in a manner that allows it to enter the environment). Supervisory Agency (LVV) written reply, June 2026.

transport.why: R. rattus is not a CITES species (Finnish Environment Institute, June 2026), so the bar is not CITES. But because keeping the animal in Finland is prohibited as an alien species, there is no lawful purpose for importing or moving one in to keep as a pet. Never release a roof rat.
transport.governing_law: No CITES (Syke, June 2026); but alien-species prohibition (§3, Act 1709/2015) bars lawful keeping, so import-to-keep has no lawful basis.

restrictions.summary: Finland's Invasive Species Act (1709/2015) §3 forbids keeping, breeding, or otherwise handling an alien species in a manner that allows it to enter the environment. The Supervisory Agency (LVV) classifies R. rattus as an alien species (EU Reg 1143/2014 definition: introduced outside its natural range; not found wild in Finland) and states (June 2026) that keeping it as a pet or breeding it is therefore not allowed. This applies even though R. rattus is on neither the EU Union list nor Finland's national invasive list (Decree 1725/2015): the §3 general prohibition reaches every alien species, not only listed ones. The fancy rat (R. norvegicus) is kept freely; the agency's position rests on R. rattus not being established in the Finnish wild.

Keeping, breeding or transferring rats at scale requires a NOTIFICATION (ilmoitus) to Ruokavirasto at least 30 days before you start: at 7 or more cages, terraria or aquaria in regular use this counts as professional/commercial activity, and at 20 or more as large-scale non-professional keeping. Below those thresholds, hobby keeping/breeding/rehoming is unregistered, subject only to the welfare standards. Filing puts the premises in the keeper register and open to welfare inspection. The threshold is the same for the fancy rat (R. norvegicus). Never release a roof rat.
steps: If at or above 7 cages (professional) or 20 cages (large-scale), file the ilmoitus to Ruokavirasto via the animal-keeper and facility register at least 30 days before commencing
Below the threshold, keep no notification is required; meet the Decree 674/2010 welfare and housing standards
restrictions.where_to_file: Ruokavirasto (Finnish Food Authority), via the animal-keeper and facility register (eläintenpitäjä- ja pitopaikkarekisteri)

restrictions.summary: Government Decree 674/2010 sets minimum housing for the rat (rotta) generically, with no distinction between R. rattus and R. norvegicus: a minimum cage floor area and height, additional floor area per group-housed animal, a continuous nest box / shelter for concealment, species-suitable substrate for digging and foraging, continuous fresh water, and a balanced diet. Falling below these is an animal welfare offence. No microchipping or registration of pet rodents is required.

inquiry_focus: (1) Is Rattus rattus (mustarotta/kattorotta) subject to any restriction under Finland's national invasive alien species decree (1725/2015) or Finland's implementation of EU Reg. 1143/2014 that would restrict keeping it as a pet, i.e., is it on the national list or not? (2) Under the Animal Welfare Act 693/2023, does the ilmoituksenvarainen eläintenpito notification for small hobby rodents such as rats trigger at 7 cages (professional) or 20 cages (large-scale), is it filed to Ruokavirasto, and is anything beyond notification required? (3) For non-commercial movement of captive-bred R. rattus from another EU member state by the owner personally, are there any species-specific documentation or health-certificate requirements?
